name: Genomes RTS — Procedural Battlefield
changes: rubble tiles now prefer Rapier heightfield colliders with resilient trimesh and cuboid runtime fallbacks
tile overflow preserves the newest deposit at its world location and merges older material instead of modulo-wrapping new debris into an unrelated tile
rubble airborne re-ejection preserves per-material volume, not only total solid volume
RubbleField exposes baked and per-material accounting while DestructionPhysics reports hero, cheap and baked representation volume together
rubble surfaces support a terrain-height provider; collision, ballistic trace, visual meshes and bake eligibility no longer assume y=0
rubble movement cost uses pile-only slope while surface normals and collision follow combined terrain plus pile geometry
near rubble detail samples local cell material mixtures instead of coloring every chunk by the tile-dominant material
benchmark harness records represented debris volume and collider modes
sleeping ground-level Rapier debris bakes into a persistent volume-conserving rubble field after a one-second grace period
active debris overflow demotes to a 1024-record cheap-airborne pool instead of deleting building material
cheap packet debris uses one pooled instanced mesh and settles into the same rubble field
0.5 m rubble cells are grouped into 4 m tiles with material mixtures, packing, local slope relaxation and a 256-tile hard cap that merges instead of deleting volume
dirty rubble tiles batch static triangle-surface collider and low-poly mound rebuilds; old rigid bodies are removed only after replacement collision exists
microscopic unrepresentable hulls and exhausted cheap-debris capacity become micro/direct rubble deposits rather than disappearing
settled rubble participates in ballistics as porous mixed-material cover and can be excavated/re-ejected by AP or HE
rubble exposes height, slope, movement cost and cover navigation hooks; destruction-demo movement already uses the movement cost
dedicated rubble conservation/cover tests and benchmark counters cover hero, cheap and baked representations
material-specific AP resistance replaces the overly permissive brittle-material tuning while preserving AP advantage against steel and armor
brick and concrete now absorb substantially more projectile work and create larger front/rear/stress zones
masonry uses a radius-driven virtual brick/mortar cluster instead of a fixed 3x3 patch
bounded adjacent wall pieces can detach as physical ejecta without increasing convex-piece count
concrete/mineral stress propagates into neighboring building sections and structural connection integrity
steel retains dent/plug/petal response classes with local bounded ejecta
wood uses grain-oriented split geometry plus grain-biased penetration and ricochet deflection
material response calibration is recorded as gameplay data, not a real-world firing table
procedural building v5 with exact stair families, layered walls, detailed openings and procedural roof/facade equipment
persistent projectile state with deterministic material-aware ricochet, glance and post-penetration deflection
projectile integrity, deformation, stability, aerodynamic degradation and bounded secondary breakup
layered wall penetration resistance and correct steel-door material mapping
bounded tapered perforation with coherent entry/exit metadata and material-specific surface damage
rounded edge/corner swept-sphere refinement after conservative broad-phase contact
progressive structural connection integrity with support-to-dependent reverse indexing
off-centre Rapier impulses for rotational rubble response
separate static-building and moving-debris BVHs with moving-only physics refresh
adaptive projectile flight segments with diagnostic flight events disabled in production mode
one-command Node/Three/Rapier test suite and manual GitHub Actions workflow while repository runners are unavailable
